question: Which of the following is the structural and functional unit of an organism?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cell**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **cell** is the basic **structural and functional unit** of all living organisms.
 
• Cells are the smallest units of life that can replicate independently, and they are often called the "building blocks of life".
 
• There are two main types of cells: **prokaryotic** cells, which lack a nucleus, and **eukaryotic** cells, which have a nucleus.
 
• Cells carry out essential functions such as energy production, nutrient processing, and waste elimination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate) is a molecule that carries energy within cells.
 
• The **mitochondria** are organelles within the cell that produce ATP through cellular respiration.
 
• The **nucleus** is an organelle in eukaryotic cells that contains most of the cell's genetic material.
 
• Cells can be specialized to perform specific functions, such as muscle cells, nerve cells, and blood cells.
